description: Team IMPULSE is six students from India, named for the signal rather than the silence. We build for the browser: 3D scenes, real-time rendering, front-end, and the writing that holds it together. For NASA Space Apps we chose "Abandoned but not Forgotten" because it is a storytelling problem disguised as a data problem — retroreflectors still answering lasers from Earth. We built a 3D web experience you can explore: click an object, learn what it was, when it was left, and why it still matters.
summary:
Space Museum is an immersive 3D virtual museum honoring NASA’s historic spacecraft left resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Instead of presenting static plaques, our project brings these dormant machines back to life through real-time bidirectional voice com-links powered by Google Gemini 3.8 Multimodal Live API.

Visitors walk freely through a 3D architectural pavilion in first-person, approaching relics like Apollo 11’s Lunar Module, Spirit & Opportunity, Viking 1, InSight, Dawn, and Ingenuity. Each spacecraft speaks in the first person with authentic telemetry, emotional warmth, and unique voice personas—allowing school-age students and enthusiasts to ask questions and hear firsthand stories of Martian dust storms, lunar landings, and scientific triumphs. Visitors can also sit in an in-world 3D cinema auditorium to screen 12 curated NASA archival documentaries directly on the auditorium wall with full 360° head-look freedom.

By transforming silent off-world equipment into interactive, talking storytellers, Space Museum bridges cutting-edge generative AI and WebGL to ensure humanity’s robotic pioneers are abandoned, but never forgotten.
details:
Project: Space Museum — Abandoned but not Forgotten

As a team primarily composed of high school students, we asked ourselves a fundamental question: Why do traditional museums and history textbooks often feel disconnected from younger generations? We found our answer in video games. Today's youth crave interactive, exploratory, and agency-driven experiences. We decided to bridge the gap between space history and interactive gaming by transforming NASA’s archival mission and rover data into an immersive 3D open-world exploration platform.

What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Space Museum places visitors inside an interactive 3D lunar and martian facility where they can:

  1. Freely Roam in First-Person: Walk, sprint, or activate drone flight mode to explore an open-concept biodome museum.
  2. 3D Artifact Exhibits: Inspect high-fidelity 3D models of legendary spacecraft (such as Opportunity, Curiosity, Sojourner, Apollo 11 Lunar Module, and Viking 1) alongside curated archival photography and telemetry metrics.
  3. Live Voice Com-Link (Relic Dialogue): Rather than reading static plaques, visitors press a button and speak in real time directly to the spacecraft. Powered by the Gemini 3.8 Multimodal Live API, the rovers reply back via voice in authentic, first-person historical personas grounded in actual NASA mission logs.
  4. In-World Archival Cinema: Walk into a built-in movie auditorium, take a luxury seat, and watch 12 high-definition archival space documentaries rendered directly onto the 3D cinema screen using CSS3D.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Emotional & Educational Connection: By giving rovers and landers a voice, history is transformed into personal narrative, helping students emotionally connect with scientific exploration and engineering resilience.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Operates smoothly directly in standard web browsers on laptops, desktops, and mobile devices without requiring heavy downloads or game installs.
  • Preserving Heritage: Honors equipment that served humanity on alien worlds, ensuring their triumphs and final transmissions are never forgotten.

Creativity & Design Considerations

We combined gaming mechanics (WASD navigation, collision physics, head-look, procedural footstep audio) with educational curation. In designing the system, we specifically considered:

  • Low Latency: Delivering instantaneous, conversational speech interaction rather than clunky text chatbot interfaces.
  • Immersion: Eliminating distracting HUD clutter and embedding documentaries directly onto 3D walls rather than external pop-ups.
  • Student Appeal: Creating a vibrant, retro-futuristic atmosphere that inspires curious minds to pursue aerospace, software engineering, and data science.

Technical Architecture & Tools

  • Frontend: Three.js (WebGL 3D rendering), CSS3DRenderer (for in-world documentary projection), HTML5/CSS3 glassmorphism UI, Vite build system, and procedural Web Audio API for environmental sound design.
  • Backend & Edge Infrastructure: Cloudflare Workers edge server running bidirectional streaming WebSockets.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google DeepMind Gemini 3.8 Multimodal Live API with custom system instructions grounding rover personalities in real telemetry, utilizing 16kHz PCM audio input and 24kHz audio synthesis.
  • 3D Modeling & CAD: Autodesk Fusion 360
  • Open Data Sources: NASA Open Data, NASA Treks elevation models, and JPL archival mission records.
  • Vs code, copilot.
  • LLM used- Gemini, CLaude, ChatGPT, Deep Seek
